Statement: Every employee of the firm who completed the certification course received a bonus this year. Ravi, an employee of the firm, did not receive a bonus this year.
Conclusions:
I. Ravi did not complete the certification course.
II. Ravi joined the firm this year.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
explanation: Had Ravi completed the course, he would have received a bonus. He did not, so he did not complete it — I follows. The statement says nothing about when Ravi joined the firm, so II does not follow.
shortcut: If A then B; not B, so not A

Statement: Notice issued by a city's traffic police: "Commuters are requested to use the newly opened metro line to reduce congestion on MG Road."
Assumptions:
I. Some commuters are likely to act on the request and use the metro line.
II. Congestion on MG Road is currently a concern for the traffic police.
Which assumption(s) are implicit in the statement?
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
explanation: A request is issued only when the authority expects at least some people to act on it, so I is implicit. Asking commuters to help reduce congestion on MG Road presumes that the congestion there is a concern, so II is also implicit.

Statement: Several students of a college hostel fell ill, and laboratory tests found that the hostel's drinking water was contaminated.
Courses of action:
I. The hostel should be closed down permanently.
II. The authorities should immediately arrange safe drinking water and get the water source cleaned and tested.
Which course(s) of action follow?
explanation: II directly addresses the identified cause — contaminated water — and is practical and immediate. Permanently closing the hostel is an extreme step that is not justified when the problem can be fixed, so I does not follow.
shortcut: A valid course of action solves the stated problem without overreacting

Statement: No candidate who scored below 60% in the written test was called for the interview. Neha was called for the interview.
Conclusions:
I. Neha was selected after the interview.
II. Every candidate who scored 60% or more in the written test was called for the interview.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
explanation: The statement says nothing about the result of the interview, so I does not follow. It only says that scoring below 60% rules a candidate out; it does not say that everyone scoring 60% or more was called, so II does not follow. (What does follow is that Neha scored at least 60%.)
